style.vernacular: Portuguese colonial port city on a bay: Baixa streets of 2-4 storey pastel-rendered buildings with wrought-iron balconies, arcades and clay-tile roofs; baroque-style whitewashed churches and 16th-17th century stone forts on the headlands; 1950s-70s modernist slabs with brise-soleil in Cidade Alta; since the 2000s oil boom, glass-and-concrete towers and waterfront (Marginal) developments; flat-roofed concrete housing and corrugated-roof musseques sprawl beyond. Dry, hazy coastal air with palms and flame trees.
style.ornament: Portuguese azulejo tile panels, calcada (black-and-white stone mosaic) pavements, curved baroque pediments over three-door church fronts, cast-iron balustrades and balconies, thick fort walls studded with cannon, Soviet-era monumental memorials, and Brazilian-style modern towers.
